title: Fairness for the People, by the People: Minority Collective Action
measurement_description: The paper measures machine learning model fairness (specifically Equalized Odds and Statistical Parity) regarding toxicity classification of online comments that mention specific religious identities. It evaluates how 'algorithmic collective action' (strategic label flipping by minority users) can mitigate unfair bias against these religious groups.
findings: The study found that strategic collective action by a minority group (e.g., flipping text toxicity labels) can substantially reduce unfairness metrics like Equalized Odds violations in classifiers trained on comments mentioning Christians and Muslims. The proposed 'Rank by probability' (RB-prob) method achieved higher fairness efficiency—requiring fewer label flips to improve fairness—with minimal impact on overall prediction error compared to random label flipping.
references: Solon Barocas and Andrew D. Selbst. Big data's disparate impact. California Law Review, 104(3): 671–732, 2016.
